sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Merchandising of Fashion Jewelry and Fine Timepieces

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526 of 1999 (UIAF), Law 1121 of 2006, Law 1762 of 2015, Law 2010 of 2019, DIAN Resolution No. 000164 of 2021, and Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia Circular 001 of 2020.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation representation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of residence of each foreign shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or corporate existence of foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry in the shareholder's home country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copy and proof of address for each shareholder, director, and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Consular section of the Colombian embassy or consulate of the shareholder's residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, legal representatives, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists, European Union Consolidated List, and the Colombian consolidated UIAF/SIJIN watchlists. A formal AML/CFT policy consistent with Law 1121 of 2006 and Circular 001 of 2020 must be established before banking and commercial registry activation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) via www.rues.org.co and the competent local Cámara de Comercio
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All business names must be registered in Spanish using the Latin alphabet without diacritical marks for registry indexing. Foreign-origin names must be transliterated phonetically and must comply with the Ley 1258 of 2008 restrictions on misleading, confusing, or identical names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of a name rejection, the applicant may file a 'recurso de reposición' with the corresponding Chamber of Commerce within 10 business days of notification. If rejected again, a 'recurso de apelación' may be filed with the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) within the following 10 business days. The applicant may simultaneously reserve a new distinct name without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for company registry and tax domicile purposes provided a physical address is designated to receive judicial notices and DIAN communications. For ISIC 4791 e-commerce operators in jewelry, watches, and fashion, banks and payment processors (Stripe and PayPal) may require a more conventional physical presence or documented sublease arrangement for effective KYC and enhanced due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate, approximately 20% within the first year of operation. DIAN automated risk scoring and municipal inspection protocols can flag high-value goods merchants for unannounced on-site verification of inventory and commercial substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio competent for the proposed registered address
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee per Cámara de Comercio tariff schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial authentication of the SAS incorporation document and by-laws
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff schedule for private documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Chamber of Commerce registration of the company and commercial establishment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff based on declared capital and activity, approximately 0.7% of capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: DIAN RUT pre-registration and UBO Register (RUB) support filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: DIAN (Unidad Administrativa Especial Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee; administrative support and attorney fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/OFAC/UN PEP and sanctions screening through third-party database
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for UBO trace and sanctions screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille of foreign corporate documents and sworn translation into Spanish
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and duly certified Colombian translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory apostille fee and standard certified translation tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Local counsel pre-incorporation legal review and drafting of governance documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for SAS formation and compliance review

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Código de Comercio arts. 110, 353-356, Decreto 1074 de 2015 (mercantile registry), Decreto 2155 de 2021 (simplified registry tariffs)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) acting through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (or Escritura Pública if real property is contributed) endorsed by a certified lawyer and filed on the Formulario Único de Registro Empresarial
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an S.A.S.; capital may be minimal and is freely fixed by the bylaws, with at least one subscribed share. Any unpaid balance of subscribed shares must be paid within a maximum of two (2) years. Cash contributions must be evidenced by a bank deposit certificate or an accountant's sworn certification; no escrow account is statutorily mandated, though contributed funds must remain traceable in a Colombian corporate bank account. Non-resident shareholders may hold 100% of the shares.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the subscription and payment schedule of the S.A.S. authorized capital are hereby approved, each founder's subscription being recorded in Article 5 of the bylaws. FURTHER RESOLVED: that the corporation's registered address shall be [Address, City, Colombia] effective immediately, and any relocation shall require a general assembly resolution. FURTHER RESOLVED: that [Appointee Name], Passport No. [No.], is appointed sole Legal Representative with full statutory powers under Ley 1258/2008 and the bylaws, and [Appointee Name] is appointed alternate officer. FURTHER RESOLVED: that the Legal Representative is instructed to register the company with the Chamber of Commerce, DIAN, municipal treasury, labor-risk insurers, and to open bank accounts and execute e-commerce platform agreements. Approved unanimously by the founding shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name availability verification and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social through the RUES virtual registry window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the RUES online portal, submit the homonymy consultation (certificado de homonimia) for the proposed corporate name, and request a provisional name reservation for thirty (30) calendar days. Verify that the proposed activity codes (CIUU 4791 - retail e-commerce of jewelry and watches) are covered in the business object clause.
required_dossiers: Subscribers' valid identification or passport copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is preempted by an existing merchant, the applicant may file an alternative name request or appeal to the Chamber of Commerce within five (5) business days; the reservation may be renewed once.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution, notarization and electronic signature of the incorporation instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público for public deed execution; independent lawyer's certification (certificación de abogado) for private document form
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the bylaws (estatutos) of the S.A.S. including the business object for online merchandising of fashion jewelry and timepieces, share classes, capital payment schedule, and management structure. Have the founding shareholders sign the private incorporation document; if contributions include real estate or assets in kind, execute before a notary as escritura pública. The certifying attorney must attest that the document complies with Ley 1258/2008.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if a non-resident shareholder is represented
Proof of capital payment (bank certificate) if paid-in at execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or certifying counsel detects defective clauses, the parties may amend the instrument and re-execute without penalty; no limit applies on number of re-executions before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Chamber of Commerce registration and issuance of the Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (RUES filing window and physical service points)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the signed incorporation instrument, the single registry form (Formulario Único de Registro Empresarial - FUE), and the pre-RUT data; pay the registration tariff (derechos de inscripción) and the departmental registration tax (impuesto de registro at 0.7% on subscribed capital). Upon registration, obtain the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal and the Matrícula Mercantil evidencing the legal representative's registered signature.
required_dossiers: Payment receipt of registry tariff and registration tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues a correction requirement (requerimiento), the company must remedy within ten (10) working days by submitting an amended instrument; failure to cure voids the filing, but a fresh filing under the same NIT pre-assignment is permitted without losing corporate identity benefits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration and electronic invoicing authorization with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales, Sede Electrónica / portal Muisca
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company in the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) to obtain the definitive NIT, selecting the income tax, VAT (IVA) responsibility for e-commerce retail, and the electronic invoicing obligation (facturación electrónica). The Legal Representative must obtain an electronic signature certificate and link it to the corporate RUT for future returns and e-invoicing submissions.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
RUT preliminary form generated by the Chamber
Legal representative's identification and electronic signature certificate
Proof of registered address (utility bill or lease)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN assigns an incorrect tax status or responsibilities, file the electronic rectification (trámite RUT - actualización) through Muisca within ten (10) business days; attach the certificate of existence and municipal zoning certificate to cure address verification refusals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal registration for ICA tax and land use approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda or municipal treasury; Secretaría de Planeación for use-of-soil certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company in the municipal industry and commerce tax roll (Impuesto de Industria y Comercio - ICA) under activity code 4791, file the declaration for e-commerce sales, and obtain the Certificado de Uso de Suelo for the administrative office or warehouse. The registration is a precondition for invoicing Colombian customers.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Lease contract or ownership title of the registered premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the land use certificate denies commercial operation at the address, relocate the registered address to a commercially zoned property or file a change-of-use petition with the planning authority; the ICA registration remains portable upon address amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire safety and occupational risk clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos de la localidad; Administradoras de Riesgos Laborales (ARL) authorized by the Ministry of Labor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the annual Certificado de Seguridad Humana from the local fire department after inspection of fire extinguishers, emergency exits, smoke detection, and evacuation signage. Simultaneously affiliate all employees with an ARL occupational risk insurer and file the basic occupational health and safety program (SG-SST) for the physical premises.
required_dossiers: List of employees and payroll registry entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection produces an unfavorable concept, execute the corrective orders and schedule a re-inspection within thirty (30) days; submitting the inspection request blocks municipal closure orders until resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Consumer protection and e-commerce compliance registration with SIC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) - Delegatura de Protección al Consumidor and data protection registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt and publish on the digital storefront the mandatory e-commerce terms: company identification, NIT, contact address, price transparency, shipping and return policy, warranty terms for jewelry and timepieces, and withdrawal right per Circular Única SIC Title II. If processing more than 20,000 consumer records, register the databases in the Registro Nacional de Bases de Datos and appoint a data protection officer.
required_dossiers: Product safety and hallmark compliance declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIC issues a preventive order regarding misleading claims (e.g., gold purity or watch brand references), submit a compliance plan within twenty (20) working days, provide certificates of origin for precious metals, and withdraw non-conforming descriptions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account opening and AML/financial integrity framework
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank's compliance officer; UIAF - Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero via the SIREL port
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate checking account in a Colombian bank in the name of the S.A.S., presenting the corporate existence certificate and the legal representative's registration. Given the Medium-Risk AML tier, adopt a written KYC policy for customers; if assets or income exceed 30,000 UVT, formalize the SAGRILAFT self-management and anti-money laundering program and report to UIAF as required.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Legal representative identification and banking signature form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank compliance unit requests additional information, provide the certified corporate registry excerpt and the final beneficiary declaration; escalate to the Chamber of Commerce to certify the corporate file if the account opening is unduly delayed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) - Delegatura de Protección al Consumidor; municipal treasury for the ICA mercantile registration and land-use certification
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Matrícula de Industria y Comercio (ICA tax registration) together with the Certificado de Uso de Suelo and the annual fire safety certificate (Certificado de Seguridad Humana de Bomberos)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) for national-level projects; Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente or regional environmental authority (CAR) for local waste management supervision
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a formal EIA for pure e-commerce retail of jewelry and watches; only a simplified environmental registration is expected if the warehouse generates more than 10 kg/month of non-hazardous packaging waste, requiring compliance with municipal solid waste ordinances and Resolution 1407 de 2018 on extended producer responsibility for packaging
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial wastewater discharge for the e-commerce operation; if a watch-repair workshop operates, VOC emissions must comply with Resolution 909 de 2008 limits and spent oil/solvent disposal must follow Decreto 1076 de 2015 hazardous waste rules; packaging cardboard and plastic must be separated for recycling under the national recycling target scheme

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: annual certificate from the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos confirming portable extinguishers, smoke detectors, unobstructed exits, and an evacuation plan for the commercial office/warehouse. Structural: municipal land-use certificate evidencing that the premises withstand commercial load and, if a jewelry safe or vault is installed, a structural load inspection by the planning authority. Occupational: mandatory ARL affiliation for all employees, an elementary Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SST) program, and product safety clearance under SIC rules on lead, cadmium, and nickel release for jewelry items offered to consumers.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (IVA - Impuesto sobre las Ventas)

mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación - DEX) lodged in DIAN's electronic customs module (MUISCA), with 'levante' clearance
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / international courier consignment note evidencing physical exit from Colombian customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (Declaración de Cambio - Formulario No. 1) issued by an authorized foreign-exchange intermediary evidencing channelization of proceeds

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Bank of the Republic of Colombia), the central monetary and exchange authority, acting in coordination with the Comité de Cambios (Foreign Exchange Committee) and the Ministerio de Hacienda y Crédito Público (Ministry of Finance and Public Credit); AML/CFT supervision is discharged by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (Financial Superintendency) and the Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero (UIAF). The operative foreign-exchange rulebook is Banco de la República External Resolution No. 1 of 2018, as amended, compiled in Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83, with DIAN (National Tax and Customs Directorate) enforcing fiscal, customs, and foreign-trade procedural aspects.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia maintains a managed floating exchange-rate regime with full current-account convertibility of the Colombian peso (COP); there are no exchange controls on trade settlements, service payments, or profit remittances. However, all transactions must be executed through the regulated 'mercado cambiario' using authorized intermediary banks and financial corporations. Capital-account inflows, including direct foreign investment into the S.A.S., are permitted without prior licensing but are subject to mandatory declaration and registration with Banco de la República (Registro Internacional de Inversiones) through the receiving bank on the statutory Declaración de Cambio (Formulario No. 5). Registration is a legal condition precedent for future dividend distributions, capital repatriation, and disinvestment remittances; unregistered capital is not lawfully remittable. The practical hurdles to profit repatriation are documentary: maintained audited financial statements, a corporate distribution resolution, payment of corporate income tax and applicable dividend withholding taxes (10% standard or treaty-reduced rate), an updated RUT, and a registered investment reflecting the original contribution at the official exchange rate. No prior central-bank approval is required once these conditions are satisfied.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombian law requires statutory 'canalización' (channeling and surrender) of 100% of export proceeds through the authorized foreign-exchange market via an authorized intermediary, with no discretionary offshore retention ratio. For goods exports, collection and surrender must be completed within the agreed commercial credit term but in no case later than 13 months after the declared maturity date of the respective export declaration; for services, the statutory window is 6 months after completion of the service. Advance payments are likewise canalized within the corresponding term. Exporters may temporarily credit proceeds to a foreign-currency account opened with an authorized bank and registered with Banco de la República, but the funds must ultimately be converted to COP or applied to specifically permitted uses within the same statutory period. Non-compliance constitutes a financial-currency offense actionable by Banco de la República and generates UIAF filings, DIAN audit adjustments, and blockage of subsequent import payments and outward remittances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente); Capital Escrow Account facility available for subscription deposits

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Itaú Colombia S.A. (formerly Itaú CorpBanca Colombia)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury or banking channel. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, and similar unlicensed electronic-money institutions) are not authorized intermediaries under Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83 and cannot lawfully execute Colombian foreign-exchange channeling or hold the S.A.S.'s statutory export proceeds. They are viable only as an ancillary collection rail for retail marketplace settlements (e.g., Stripe and PayPal payouts), provided balances are periodically swept into the Colombian operational account and the underlying export or service receipts are duly canalized and declared. Primary reliance on any unlicensed EMI would breach the surrender rules, generate UIAF suspicious-transaction signals, and cause tier-1 Colombian banks to reject clearing relationships; therefore regulatory viability is Low.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is de facto mandatory for a non-resident-owned S.A.S. in the jewelry and e-commerce sector. Tier-1 banks require at least one in-branch visit by the legal representative or by a local attorney-in-fact holding a notarized, apostilled, Spanish-translated general power of attorney registered with the Cámara de Comercio, for identity verification, signature registry, and a live SAGRILAFT/'Conozca a su Cliente' interview. Remote-only onboarding is generally declined for first-time foreign-owned accounts presenting a Medium-Risk profile; some banks (Bancolombia, Banco de Bogotá) permit digitally initiated filings, but final approval still depends on an in-person executive or representative appearance in Bogotá, Medellín, or Cali. Full digital onboarding without any physical anchor is not a realistic compliance-safe path.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: e-commerce of fine timepieces and fashion jewelry is inherently categorised as higher-risk AML/CTF activity ('joyería y metales preciosos'), exposing the account to payment-laundering and cash-equivalent typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete supply-chain and custody file: accredited supplier pro-forma and commercial invoices; gemological or manufacture certificates of authenticity (GIA-type grading for stones and chronometric certification for watches); customs import declarations (Declaración de Importación) with DIAN status; shipping documents and cargo insurance; and an internally adopted AML/CTF program aligned with Circular Externa 026/2023 (SAGRILAFT) containing transaction monitoring thresholds, customer due-diligence procedures, and a documented risk matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Banking-profile mismatch: the account will receive aggregated Stripe and PayPal settlement payouts from multiple foreign merchant platforms, producing a high-velocity, intermingled cash-flow pattern that is difficult to reconcile to retail books of record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Triple-layer reconciliation bundle: executed payment-processing agreements with Stripe, Inc. and PayPal Holdings; platform payout statements (daily or weekly aggregated files) imported into the S.A.S. ERP; and a sales-order-level reconciliation certificate signed by the company controller, together with refund and chargeback logs and the e-commerce checkout system's transaction report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: ordinary corporate extracts name only foreign shareholders and representatives whose beneficial-ownership chain has not been vetted under Colombian SAGRILAFT standards, preventing the bank from completing enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and legalized corporate records from the home jurisdiction (certificate of incorporation, registry extract, certificate of incumbency); notarized UBO identification forms listing every natural person holding 10% or more; passport copies of those persons; an illustrated group ownership tree; and a stamped UBO declaration or Colombian legal opinion confirming the ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Contagion from initial capital inflow: the new account will immediately receive a cross-border equity injection and possibly shareholder loans from multiple jurisdictions, which banks classify as higher-risk source-of-funds transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds memorandum comprising: notarized capital-subscription minutes or written shareholder loan agreements stating interest and repayment terms; independent confirmation of the investor's bank account and prior cleared activity; the inbound MT103 wire references and bank debits; a disclosed 90-day funding and settlement plan; and a commitment to quarantine the first tranche for a minimum of 30 days after clearance before any disbursement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward equity and shareholder-loan proceeds are wired by SWIFT MT103 from the investor's own bank account to the S.A.S. operational account at the Colombian clearing bank. The instruction must reference the beneficiary NIT and account number, state the concept in Spanish (e.g., 'Aporte de capital — inversión extranjera directa' or 'Préstamo entre compañías'), and avoid third-party beneficiaries or mixed-currency flows. The receiving bank issues the statutory Declaración de Cambio on Formulario No. 5 and files the investment registration with Banco de la República under Decree 1192/2021 before funds are fully credited; the resulting international-investment registry entry, rather than the wire itself, is the operative legal document that later permits dividend remittances, loan amortizations, and disinvestment exits. For intercompany loans, the bank requires the loan agreement, confirmation of interest-rate compliance with Colombian ceiling rules, and registration of the external credit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outward trade payments are cleared through the S.A.S. Colombian account via (i) SWIFT MT103 direct outward remittances for open-account imports of gems, components, and finished timepieces, or (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) issued by the Colombian bank in favor of foreign suppliers. Each disbursement must be matched to the corresponding import declaration (Declaración de Importación), commercial invoice, transport document (bill of lading or airway bill), and, for LC settlements, a complying documentary presentation; the bank records the outflow in the Declaración de Cambio on the import-of-goods form with the correct economic-concept code. Freight charges, platform commissions (Stripe/PayPal), and cross-border service fees are cleared under the applicable services codes on the same rail. To preserve clean FX history, all outflows should emanate from the same account that receives export channels, and LC issuance requires a signed application, guarantee facilities, and in certain circumstances cash cover.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC forward contracts (Forwards COP/USD) executed with authorized intermediaries to hedge import costs, payroll, and intercompany obligations arising from genuine commercial exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) to hedge non-COP foreign-currency collections (EUR, USD) where the underlying invoice or receivable evidences real economic exposure
Cross-currency swaps (permutas de moneda) with commercial banks to manage long-dated trade-finance and receivable/payable mismatches
FX options (call/put) transacted over-the-counter or through the Colombian exchange (Derivex) as covered, risk-reducing strategies tied to forecast cash flows
Standardized USD/COP futures cleared by the Colombian Stock Exchange (Derivex) where economically justified and matched to the S.A.S. underlying trade flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Mercantile Registration Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (local Chamber of Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 for the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee accrues daily after March 31; continued non-renewal for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off, suspension of corporate rights, and possible dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statement Filing (Estados Financieros) accompanied by management and audit/revisor fiscal reports
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio; DIAN if required for consolidated or tax-reporting purposes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approved by shareholders' general assembly no later than March 31; filed with the Chamber of Commerce within 10 days of approval and by April 30 at the latest
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file financial statements blocks annual renewal and may result in cancellation of commercial registration; monetary sanctions and prohibition of commercial activities may apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' General Assembly Minutes (Acta de Asamblea de Accionistas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Statutory minute book (internal record, not filed unless requested)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held within three months of fiscal year-end (by March 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct fine, but inability to approve financial statements and renewal; potential shareholder liability for unauthorized continuation of corporate activities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Unidad de Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between May 1 and June 30, according to DIAN's calendar based on the company's NIT last digit; also required after any ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to COP 20 million (approx. USD 5,000); inability to undergo tax procedures or annual renewal until corrected.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit (revisor fiscal) mandatory if: total assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV (approx. USD 1.5 million), annual gross revenue exceeds 5,000 SMMLV, employee headcount exceeds 15, or the entity is a parent company or subject to government supervision. Otherwise audit is optional.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian GAAP pursuant to Decreto 2420/2015; full IFRS (Group 1) for large entities, IFRS for SMEs (Group 2) for typical mid-market S.A.S., and simplified 'Micro-enterprise' standards (Group 3) for entities with assets below 500 SMMLV.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: S.A.S. must confirm ultimate beneficial owners annually to DIAN via the UBO registry (RUB within the 'Beneficiarios Finales' portal). Ownership transfers must be reported as they occur. Non-resident shareholders must provide updated passport, tax ID, and proof of chain of ownership where a foreign parent exists; failure to update within the May–June window results in the penalties above.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Libro de Junta Directiva)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400–1,200 annually depending on notarial support, corporate minutes, and UBO reporting
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800–2,500 for optional independent review; USD 2,500–6,000 for mandatory statutory audit with revisor fiscal

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Colombian general corporate income tax rate is 35%. The 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada' (S.A.S.) is taxed as an ordinary corporation on worldwide income, subject to the territoriality rules of the Colombian tax system. Income derived from the online sale of fashion jewelry and fine timepieces sourced in Colombia is subject to tax. Taxpayers may access the following main incentives: (i) deduction of 100% of investments in research, technological development, and innovation projects approved by the National Innovation Authority; (ii) discounted taxable income for investments in creative industries including up to 165% deduction for certain digital and software-related assets, applicable to qualifying e-commerce platforms and technological investments; (iii) VAT discounts (IVA 19%) on qualifying fixed assets and real productive investments; and (iv) the special tax-free savings and investment mechanisms under Colombian law. No general tax holiday exists for onshore retail e-commerce activities. The effective rate can be reduced by available deductions, double-tax treaty credits, and the non-taxable status of certain foreign-source income (dividends and capital gains from foreign subsidiaries may be exempt if subject to equivalent taxation abroad).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 110 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) filed electronically through the DIAN portal (SIEV – Servicios Informáticos Electrónicos)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed by the statutory deadline set by the DIAN each year, generally within the period from August up to early October following the taxable year-end (fiscal year 31 December), according to the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT. The return and any payable tax must be submitted electronically by the due date individually assigned by DIAN Resolution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Form identification: NIT, tax year, taxpayer type, economic activity code (CIIU 4791), and filing group.
Gross income from the business activity: all revenues from online sales of fashion jewelry and watches, including export and e-commerce sales, net of discounts, returns, and allowances.
Cost of sales and inventory valuation: purchases of finished goods, costs incident to e-commerce fulfillment, shipping, packaging, special customs duties, and inventory adjustments.
Operating and administrative expenses: logistics, digital platform commissions (Stripe/PayPal), marketing, rent, salaries and social contributions, cloud infrastructure, and technology costs.

Total deductible costs and expenses subject to limits: confirmation that all deductions comply with causal, necessity, proportionality, and bankarization requirements (payments exceeding COP 18,037,000 or USD 4,500 disbursed via electronic banking).
Taxable income before adjustments: accounting net profit reconciled with tax base.
Non-taxable income and exempt income: foreign dividends meeting participation thresholds, capital gains, and treaty-protected income.
Tax losses claimed from prior years: up to a five-year carryforward, subject to the ministerial formula and re-computation rules for net equity and prior losses.
Taxable income after excesses and exemptions: resulting base for the 35% headline rate.
Corporate income tax at 35%: application of statutory rate to the taxable base and any special taxable components.
Additional taxes: possible surcharge applicable to certain industries (none applied for retail e-commerce); computation of the temporary 'Tributo a la equidad' or other levies if in force.
Tax credits and withholdings: DIAN withholding tax certificates, foreign tax credits, and other credits deducted from total tax.
Total tax payable or balance in favor: final net tax liability, subject to advance payment installments.
Advance tax installments (anticipos) for the following taxable year: 100% of the current year's net tax payable.
Equity information and previous-year tax reconciliation: declaration of net equity, gross assets, liabilities, and information returns.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a penalty equal to 5% of the taxpayer's greater gross income for the period, multiplied by the months of delay, subject to a minimum of 10 UVT per month and a maximum ceiling of 100% of the unpaid tax. Where no tax is due, the penalty is 5% of gross income subject to UVT limits; failure to file can also trigger automatic official assessment by DIAN and a sanction of 10% of the value of omissions. Late payment accrues daily interest (intereses moratorios) calculated at the effective interest rate certified by DIAN, approximately 1% to 1.5% per month, plus additional penalties and possible criminal prosecution for inaccurate returns if fraud is established.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividends distributed to Colombian resident shareholders are subject to a 35% income tax at the corporate level and a taxable dividend base for shareholders; dividends paid to non-residents and nationals are subject to an additional 10% withholding tax on the amount received after the 35% corporate tax (effective overall 41.5% on pre-tax profits). Non-resident beneficiaries are also subject to a 35% withholding tax on qualifying dividends if the distribution exceeds the taxed corporate profits base ('dividend excess' rules).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Colombia follows the OECD Model Tax Treaty framework in numerous Double Taxation Agreements. To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the competent tax authority of the residence country, issued for the corresponding calendar year; (2) provide a duly completed and apostilled Form (if applicable) certifying beneficial ownership of the income and no abuse of the treaty; (3) submit evidence of economic substance and effective establishment in the residence jurisdiction; and (4) file the withholding tax declaration in the DIAN portal with reduced rates entered. Colombia applies a 'limitation on benefits' clause in most modern DTAs. A reduced dividend withholding rate under a DTA (often 5%-15% if 10% or 25% shareholding thresholds are satisfied, and subject to holding-period requirements) is applied only after DIAN approval through the treaty relief procedure (offset of refunds or reduced withholding certification).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Technical services, royalties, software licensing, and know-how paid to non-resident related parties are subject to a 15% withholding tax on gross payments, in addition to the national VAT on digital services where applicable. Interest paid abroad to financial institutions or related lenders is subject to a 15% withholding tax (increased to 15%-20% if the lender is located in a non-cooperative jurisdiction). Treaty rates under Colombia's DTA network generally reduce royalty withholding to 10% or 5% and interest to 10%-12%, conditional on beneficial ownership, local substance, and anti-abuse provisions (BEPS Minimum Standards).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The mandatory Transfer Pricing Local File thresholds apply when consolidated gross income from the taxable year exceeds COP 1,500,000,000 (approximately USD 360,000) OR when total assets exceed COP 4,500,000,000 (approximately USD 1,080,000) at year-end. A Master File is required when total consolidated gross income exceeds COP 4,500,000,000 (approximately USD 1,080,000). For taxpayers within the e-commerce category (online merchandising of jewelry/watches), the schedular thresholds are aligned with DIAN Resolution 001 and Decree 2120.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia applies the 'substance-over-form' doctrine and a General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) under the Law 1819 of 2016. For entities carrying out digital e-commerce, DIAN scrutinizes: (i) effective management and control in Colombian territory; (ii) payroll, operational decision-making, and fulfillment infrastructure in Colombia; (iii) actual economic activity as distinguished from a mere letterbox; (iv) permanent establishment exposure for foreign-related digital sellers. Although Colombia is not a Caribbean Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) jurisdiction, entities incorporated as S.A.S. trading online must maintain full economic substance and real presence to avoid being characterized as a shell, and to access treaty benefits. The OECD BEPS Action 5 framework applies for exchange of information; artificial arrangements stripping Colombian-source income trigger re-characterization and significant sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-reporting of e-commerce revenues, concealing Stripe/PayPal settlements, use of foreign shell accounts, or falsifying accounting records to avoid corporate income tax, VAT, or withholding tax of non-resident suppliers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction for tax evasion carries imprisonment of 4 to 9 years plus a fine equal to 200% to 1000% of the evaded tax (Law 1819 of 2016, Article 333). Administrative evasion penalties range from 20% to 160% of the omitted tax plus daily late interest; DIAN can impose a 1% monthly surcharge capped at 100%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, managers, and legal representatives are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes, penalties and interest when they fail to withhold or cause the non-payment (Article 794-2 Código Fiscal). In fraud cases, criminal liability extends to the actual management; courts may impose travel bans, asset freezing, and personal seizure of real property; conviction bars directors from managing legal entities and can include imprisonment for up to 9 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the S.A.S. as an artificial intermediary with no substantive management, negligible payroll, no physical or digital infrastructure in Colombia, and routing sales through conduit entities to misuse DTA benefits and hide Colombian-source e-commerce income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN re-characterizes the transactions under the GAAR; disallows deductions and treaty benefits; imposes a 160% penalty on the higher tax assessed and a potential 100% surcharge on omitted withholdings; the entity may be liquidated if its sole purpose is tax evasion (Código de Comercio Art. 19 and GAAR rules).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Shareholders and directors face 'veil piercing' under Colombian law when the corporate form is used to evade tax (Ley 1258 de 2008, SAS regime permits veil-piercing for abuse of entity purpose or fraud); directors are ordered to pay the entire tax, penalties, and interest; courts can issue travel bans and freeze personal assets; risk of criminal liability for criminal association.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting payments in jewelry/watches e-commerce without implementing a risk-based AML compliance program, failing to report suspicious transactions, structuring transactions to evade reporting thresholds, or using digital payment rails to launder proceeds from unlawful commerce.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 1121 of 2006, the Superintendencia de Sociedades imposes fines up to COP 50,000,000 (approximately USD 12,000) per violation, increased to 1% of annual revenues for serious offenses; DIAN and the UIAF can suspend the entity’s commercial registration and prohibit operations; aggravated money laundering carries imprisonment of 10 to 30 years and fines from 1,000 to 50,000 minimum monthly wages (Law 1762 of 2015).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who fail to install AML controls or who knowingly process illegal proceeds are criminally liable as co-authors; they face imprisonment, monetary penalties, and civil restitution to harmed third parties; a travel ban is commonly applied pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the Informative Declaration of Transfer Pricing (Form 120) by the statutory deadline, failure to prepare Local/Master Files, or pricing cross-border purchases of jewelry, watches, technology services, or management fees not at arm's length, thereby shifting Colombian profits to foreign related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalty per Form 120: 10% of the value of the related party transactions up to 200 UVT per infraction; failure to submit documentation: 1% of related-party turnover per month up to 5% of turnover (minimum 100 UVT and maximum 12,000 UVT); adjustments to taxable income based on DIAN's OECD-compliant pricing method plus a 10% to 20% punitive surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative is personally liable for declaring false information or signing the transfer pricing return without reasonable grounds; DIAN may impose joint liability for the tax deficiency up to the amount of the benefit obtained; criminal indictment for aggravated fraud can follow if the false documentation is used to evade tax.
